metas.name: Coherence
metas.description: Captures an inversion problem in film form: eight people at a dinner party during a comet find other houses holding the same eight people, and try to tell the worlds apart with numbered photos, dice and glow sticks — markers that keep getting copied or lost.

metas.name: Enemy
metas.description: Captures two men who are observably identical. A Toronto history professor finds an actor who is his exact double — same face, scar and voice — and no measurement he can run separates them, so the film lets the ambiguity stay open.

metas.name: Primer
metas.description: Captures nested causal chains in parallel. Two engineers build a time machine in a garage, copies of the same people multiply across loops, and who is observing whom keeps flipping depending on which loop you are in.

metas.name: Predestination
metas.description: Captures a closed loop where a self is its own cause. A time-travelling agent on one last assignment is caught in a cycle that lands on the autonomy paradox: if the self seeking freedom was produced by the structure, what would escaping be for that self?

metas.name: Children of Men
metas.description: Captures a society coming apart at street level. In 2027, after 18 years of human infertility, a burned-out bureaucrat must get one pregnant woman across a collapsing Britain of refugee camps and long-take ambushes.

metas.name: Sorcerer
metas.description: Captures pure physical tension. Four fugitives in South America take the only job out — hauling unstable nitroglycerin in old trucks through jungle — centred on getting a truck across a rotting rope bridge in a storm, in real time.

metas.name: Memories of Murder
metas.description: Captures investigators failing, for real. South Korea's first serial murder case, 1986: local cops who beat confessions out of people, a Seoul detective who trusts evidence, and a country equipped for neither to work.

metas.name: Come and See
metas.description: Captures war as it is done to a child. Belarus, 1943: a boy joins the partisans beaming and ages a lifetime in days; it is not the gore, it is his face.

metas.name: Uncut Gems
metas.description: Captures gambling mania as perpetual motion. A New York jeweller owes everyone and keeps placing the next bet to fix the last one; the film never lets him or you breathe for two hours.

metas.name: Persona
metas.description: Captures what happens when one person stops speaking and the other can't stop. A mute actress, her nurse, a summer house, and the boundary between them getting porous.

metas.name: Perfect Blue
metas.description: Captures fame eating a person's grip on which self is hers. A pop idol turned actress, a stalker, and a fan site narrating her life in first person — the animated form is what makes the slippage work.

metas.name: Heat
metas.description: Captures professionalism as a whole identity, on both sides of the law. A robber and a detective each incapable of a life outside the work, recognising themselves in each other over coffee.

metas.name: No Country for Old Men
metas.description: Captures an older moral world realising it no longer applies. A man finds drug money, a killer flips coins, and a sheriff narrates his own obsolescence; it goes quiet exactly where other thrillers go loud.

metas.name: Cure
metas.description: Captures emptiness spreading from person to person. A Tokyo detective investigates murders where each killer is different, calm, and cannot explain themselves — hypnotic and grey rather than jumpy.

metas.name: Lake Mungo
metas.description: Captures grief in the form of a family documentary. Found footage, but the subject is not the ghost — it is parents and a brother in interviews, months after a drowning, still looking for anything.

metas.name: Hereditary
metas.description: Captures a family where grief and resentment were already there before anything supernatural. A grandmother dies, a mother builds miniature scenes of her life, and a dinner-table argument is the scariest sequence.

metas.name: Le Samouraï
metas.description: Captures cool as ritual and solitude. A Paris hitman in a trench coat, a grey room, a bird in a cage, an alibi arranged like furniture — almost no psychology given, all behaviour.

metas.name: Thief
metas.description: Captures a craftsman trying to buy a normal life with one last job. A Chicago safecracker with a collage of his dream life in his wallet, neon and rain, tools on metal filmed like jewellery-making.

metas.name: Dog Day Afternoon
metas.description: Captures a bank robbery becoming a live street spectacle. One hot Brooklyn afternoon, Pacino working the crowd outside like a rally, and the reason for the robbery arriving piece by piece.

metas.name: The Conversation
metas.description: Captures a man whose job is listening realising he has finally heard something. A surveillance expert replays one taped conversation until a line changes meaning, and his own privacy obsession turns on him.

metas.name: Thelma & Louise
metas.description: Captures escape becoming irreversible, and friendship becoming absolute. A weekend trip, a parking lot, a gun — then two women driving west, getting freer and more cornered in the same scenes.

metas.name: Meek's Cutoff
metas.description: Captures being lost, from the women's side of the wagons. Oregon Trail settlers, a guide who may be bluffing, water running out — long shots of bonnets and horizon where the drama is thirst and waiting.

metas.name: Army of Shadows
metas.description: Captures resistance as cold, lonely procedure. French Resistance, 1942: safe houses, coded phrases, informers executed badly — no glamour and almost no hope, filmed like a heist movie in mourning.

metas.name: The Night of the Hunter
metas.description: Captures childhood danger as a fairy tale. A preacher with LOVE and HATE tattooed on his knuckles hunts two children down a river for hidden money; they flee by boat through a dreamlike, animal-watched night.

metas.name: All the President's Men
metas.description: Captures journalism as shoe leather. Watergate as phone calls, parking garages, notebooks and editors asking 'what else do you have?' — verification repeated until a presidency moves.

metas.name: The Insider
metas.description: Captures the cost of telling the truth inside two corporations at once. A tobacco scientist bound by confidentiality, a TV producer with a network to protect, and an interview everyone with money wants buried.

metas.name: Zodiac
metas.description: Captures obsession with a case that will not close. San Francisco, years of codes, files, basements and false certainties; the killer fades and the men who chased him are what's left damaged.

metas.name: Sicario
metas.description: Captures an idealist being used as a legal fig leaf. An FBI agent attached to a border operation she is not briefed on, a convoy into Juárez filmed like an occupying army, rules revealed only after she has broken them.

metas.name: Burning
metas.description: Captures class envy curdling into a mystery with no floor. In Seoul, a delivery kid, a girl who mimes eating a tangerine so well you see it, a rich man who burns abandoned greenhouses — and a disappearance the film will not solve.

metas.name: First Reformed
metas.description: Captures despair finding a political shape inside a small church. A minister keeping a diary in a historic church that is mostly a gift shop, and a young activist asking whether God can forgive us for what we've done to the world.

metas.name: Under the Skin
metas.description: Captures human beings seen from outside the species. A woman drives a van around Glasgow picking up men, in real streets with hidden cameras and non-actors, and something in the routine begins to fail — images that lodge permanently.

metas.name: Gattaca
metas.description: Captures a caste system built from a blood sample. A man born without genetic screening borrows another man's blood, urine and identity to reach space, while his 'valid' brother keeps challenging him to swimming races neither should survive.

metas.name: Room
metas.description: Captures a child's entire world being eleven feet wide, and then it not being. A mother makes a complete, loving universe for her five-year-old inside the shed where they're held; the second half, outside, is the harder adjustment for both.

metas.name: Funny Games
metas.description: Captures the audience's appetite, by refusing to feed it the usual way. Two polite young men hold a family at their holiday house; violence happens off-screen or gets rewound, and the film keeps asking why you're still watching.

metas.name: Videodrome
metas.description: Captures a TV signal getting inside a body. A sleazy Toronto cable programmer finds a pirate broadcast of torture, becomes obsessed, and his perception and flesh start reorganising around it.

metas.name: The Lives of Others
metas.description: Captures a surveillance officer changed by the lives he's assigned to transcribe. East Berlin, 1984: a Stasi captain bugs a playwright's flat, types his reports, and quietly begins to edit what the state gets to know.

metas.name: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy
metas.description: Captures espionage as tired old men in bad rooms. A mole inside British intelligence, investigated through retirement-age sadness, Christmas parties and files — almost nothing explodes; the atmosphere is the action.

metas.name: The Third Man
metas.description: Captures friendship curdling in a ruined, divided city. Postwar Vienna: a pulp writer arrives to find his friend dead and getting saintlier the less sense the story makes — zither music, sewers, and the ferris wheel speech.

metas.name: Notorious
metas.description: Captures love being used as an intelligence asset. A woman is recruited to marry into a Nazi circle in Rio because of who her father was, by an agent unable to say the one thing that would make it bearable.

metas.name: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
metas.description: Captures Cold War spycraft as exhaustion and managed betrayal. A burnt agent is sent on one last operation that requires him to become genuinely washed up — the bleakest, most honest of the Le Carré films.

metas.name: Rififi
metas.description: Captures a robbery as manual labour. A Paris jewel heist whose centrepiece is roughly half an hour with no dialogue and no score — umbrellas, drills, plaster dust, men breathing — that every heist film since is quoting.

metas.name: The Killing
metas.description: Captures a perfect plan told in pieces that don't line up in time. A racetrack robbery replayed from each participant's angle, a suitcase of money, and an airport finale involving a small dog.

metas.name: Sexy Beast
metas.description: Captures menace arriving in a holiday villa. A retired gangster, happily fat and sunburned in Spain, and Ben Kingsley's Don Logan flying in to scream him back to London for one job — the terror is mostly conversational.

metas.name: Inside Man
metas.description: Captures a bank robbery as theatre with a purpose you have to wait for. Manhattan hostages dressed identically to the robbers, a detective and a fixer circling each other, and a heist whose real target isn't the money.

metas.name: Hell or High Water
metas.description: Captures two brothers robbing the bank that is taking their family's land. West Texas, foreclosed ranches and debt-relief billboards, and two ageing Rangers following them at the speed of talk — a western wearing a recession.

metas.name: Crash
metas.description: Captures desire re-wired through injury and machinery. After a serious collision on Toronto highways, a couple drift into a circle for whom crashes, scars and cars have become erotic — cold, deadpan and permanently controversial.

metas.name: Lust, Caution
metas.description: Captures an espionage performance becoming the real feeling it was faking. In occupied Shanghai, a student actress is assigned to seduce a collaborationist official so he can be killed, over years of mahjong games and assignations.

metas.name: In the Realm of the Senses
metas.description: Captures obsession with the outside world switched off. 1930s Japan, a hotel maid and her employer in a room, in a spiral based on a real case — explicit as claustrophobia, not titillation.

metas.name: A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night
metas.description: Captures a vampire film rebuilt from Iranian, Western and skate-punk parts. A fictional Iranian ghost town, a chador-wearing vampire on a skateboard, a drug dealer and a cat, in long black-and-white silences between bursts of pop.

metas.name: Atlantics
metas.description: Captures young men who leave by sea returning in another form. Dakar construction workers, unpaid for months, take a boat toward Spain; the film stays with the women left behind, the sea at night, and a love story conducted through possession and fever.

metas.name: Pi
metas.description: Captures obsession with a pattern, filmed on grain. A mathematician in a tiny New York apartment with computers made of junk, a number that Wall Street and a Hasidic sect both want, and migraines rendered as drill sounds.
